question: What is the primary purpose of the radiopaque strip incorporated into surgical swabs?

options.A: Allowing detection under X-ray imaging if a retention is suspected
options.B: Preventing the cotton fibers from fraying during active tissue manipulation
options.C: Providing a colored contrast against dark organs in the abdominal cavity
options.D: Enhancing the overall fluid absorption capacity of the fabric material

explanation: The radiopaque thread shows up clearly on plain radiographs, making it possible to locate a missing item without performing a blind re-exploration. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which surgical sponge is most appropriate for packing away bowel loops in a major exploratory laparotomy?
explanation: Laparotomy sponges provide the necessary surface area and absorbency to gently retract heavy abdominal organs during major cavity surgeries. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: What legal principle is frequently invoked in malpractice lawsuits involving retained surgical items?
explanation: This legal doctrine translates to the thing speaks for itself, implying that negligence is obvious when a foreign body is left inside a patient post-surgery. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: Who carries the primary professional accountability for performing surgical counts in the operating suite?

options.A: The scrub nurse and the circulating nurse

explanation: Operating room nursing staff bear the joint responsibility of counting, tracking, and verifying all soft goods used during an operative procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which task is specifically assigned to the circulating nurse during a surgical count?

options.A: Passing clean sponges straight to the operating surgeon
options.B: Sorting bloody items retrieved from the surgical incision
options.C: Recording tallied numbers onto the theatre whiteboard
options.D: Handling items directly inside the sterile operative wound

explanation: The circulating nurse remains unsterile, allowing them to document figures, manage waste bags, and communicate freely outside the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: How do the scrub nurse and circulating nurse work together to prevent counting errors?

options.A: The scrub nurse delegates all counting tasks to the surgeon at closure
options.B: They perform simultaneous visual verification and verbalize numbers aloud together
options.C: The circulating nurse counts items privately before handing them to the scrub nurse
options.D: They work independently to ensure no bias influences the final tally

explanation: A collaborative, dual-person check relies on both individuals seeing the items and hearing the count to catch discrepancies immediately. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: When must the initial baseline count of surgical swabs be completed?

options.A: Immediately after the skin incision is made
options.B: Before the surgical procedure officially begins
options.C: When the surgeon initiates deep cavity closure
options.D: As the final skin sutures are being tied

explanation: The baseline count establishes the starting quantity of all soft goods before any items enter the sterile field or patient body. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: A surgeon is about to close the abdominal fascia. What specific counting phase is required at this moment?
explanation: The first closing count must occur right as cavity closure begins to ensure no sponges were walled off inside the abdomen. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the very first step the nursing team must take when a count discrepancy is identified?

options.A: Notify the lead surgeon immediately and halt wound closure
options.B: Send the patient directly to the radiology department for a scan
options.C: Complete the surgical ticket and document the missing item later
options.D: Ask the hospital administrator to intervene in the theatre suite

explanation: Stopping closure prevents sealing a foreign item inside the patient while the team investigates the missing inventory. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: Which action is NOT appropriate when managing an unresolved swab count discrepancy?

options.A: Requesting an intraoperative plain radiograph of the patient
options.B: Conducting a thorough manual re-count of all items in the room
options.C: Inspecting waste receptacles and linen bags for hidden items
options.D: Proceeding with rapid skin closure while waiting for an X-ray

explanation: Closing the wound before locating a missing item violates safety protocols and puts the patient at severe risk of a retained surgical item. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: What environmental adjustment should be made in the operating theatre during critical swab counts?

options.A: Minimizing background noise and halting unnecessary chatter
options.B: Asking non-essential family members to step inside to assist
options.C: Dimming overhead surgical lamps to improve screen visibility
options.D: Turning off all automated monitoring equipment temporarily

explanation: Reducing auditory distractions allows the scrub and circulating nurses to concentrate fully during critical tally procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why is it important to group and store used surgical sponges in uniform quantities (such as fives)?

options.A: It facilitates rapid and accurate visual re-verification during counts
options.B: It ensures the sterilization machine can process them more quickly
options.C: It makes the disposal bags lighter for the sanitation staff to lift
options.D: It prevents the cotton fibers from drying out under theatre lights

explanation: Organizing items in predictable, uniform piles prevents counting mistakes that easily happen when looking at disordered heaps of bloody fabric. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)
